zh: 艺行哲学
en: Arting philosophy

zh: 卢德格·施瓦尔特
en: LUDGER SCHWARTE

zh: 在下文中，我想论证哲学是艺术实践的必要组成部分。
我将集中分析艺术实践，因为我不同意主流审美传统：它把产品——即审美对象——的出现视为理所当然，并集中于审美经验。相反，我想把注意力转向对艺术实践本身的分析。我想表明，艺术实践既不是生产的一种形式，也不是工作的一种形式——如果允许采用汉娜·阿伦特的区分——也不是一种表演。我还想区分
实践与其他实践形式，尤其是
实践；二者常常纠缠在一起，在实践学路径中尤其如此。
en: In what follows, I want to argue that philosophy is a necessary part of artistic practice.

I will concentrate on an analysis of artistic practice, because I am at odds with the dominant aesthetic tradition which takes the appearance of a product, the aesthetic object, for granted, and concentrates on the aesthetic experience. Instead I want to turn attention to an analysis of artistic practice as such. I want to show that artistic practice is neither a form of production, nor of work – if you allow Hannah Arendt’s distinctions – nor is it a kind of performance. And I would like to distinguish
practice from other forms of practice, notably
practice, with which it is often meshed, especially in praxeological approaches.

zh: 几乎每一种实践形式都包含某种审美要素，但艺术不止于此。我们不仅需要更好地解释一般艺术实践的特殊性——因为这是一个研究空白。集中考察艺术实践是什么、或在重新思考后可能成为什么，其主要理由是政治性的：艺术实践具有政治意义，这独立于其潜在产品或痕迹，因为它是自我决定的实验场，是自主性的训练场。
en: Almost every form of practice contains some aesthetic element, but art is more than that. It is not only that we need a better explanation for the specificity of artistic practice in general – because it is a research lacuna. The main reason to concentrate on what artistic practice is, or can be, when reconsidered, is a political one: artistic practice has a political significance, independent of its potential products or traces, for it is an experimental field of self-determination, a training ground for autonomy.

zh: 我的标题可能暗示我想用艺术征服全部哲学。这并非我的意思。我说的是艺术哲学的一个方面。我的目标不是主张哲学的审美化（有些人就是这样解读阿多诺《美学理论》这一标题的），而是表明：哲学——吉尔·德勒兹曾把它定义为概念的工程——需要成为艺术实践的一部分，以使艺术免于某种当代范式；在我看来，这种范式把艺术化约为应用艺术史或审美化的社会学。反过来说，目标也在于改变哲学（艺术哲学与美学）的实践。
en: My title might suggest that I want to conquer all philosophy with art. This is not what is meant. I am talking of an aspect of the philosophy of art. And my aim is not to argue for an aestheticization of philosophy (as some have read Adorno’s title,

), but to show that philosophy – the engineering of concepts, as Gilles Deleuze once defined it – needs to become part of artistic practice in order to save art from a particular contemporary paradigm, which, to my eyes, reduces art to applied art history or aestheticized sociology. The aim is also, in turn, to change the practice of philosophy (of art and aesthetics).

zh: 这里的动词“艺行”（arting）需要解释。在德语中，我想在英语中也是如此，名词“艺术”/
缺少一个动词形式。我们有时说“从事”“制作”或“生产”艺术。我对此不满意，于是在德语中创造了动词
。在英语中，这会是“to art”：艺行的实践，以动词不定式表达的艺术生成。亚历山大·加西亚·迪特曼把阿多诺的
一词不是译为“去审美化”，而是译为“去艺化”（de-arting）。
因此，正如存在
——去艺化，一种移出艺术领域的运动——也可能存在相反的运动：
，艺行。艺行意味着把艺术界之外的某物转化为某种艺术性的东西。那么，什么是艺术性的？
en: The verb ‘arting’ here needs explanation. In German, and I think in English, too, a verb form is missing for the noun ‘art’/
. We sometimes speak of ‘practising’ or ‘making’ or ‘producing’ art. I was dissatisfied with this and coined in German the verb
. In English, this would be ‘to art’: the practice of arting, the infinitive becoming of art. Alexander García Düttmann has translated Adorno’s expression
not as ‘de-aestheticization’ but as ‘de-arting’.
So, just as there is
– de-arting – a moving out of the realm of art, there can be the contrary movement –
, arting. Arting means to transform something outside the art world into something artistic. Now, what is artistic?

zh: 三种哲学路径曾试图解释这样一种运动。迪基的制度理论会说，某物一旦进入艺术机构，就成为艺术作品。但椅子、马桶和人也在其中，而它们并不是艺术作品。丹托的路径是说，它是对象加上解释。阿多诺则提出要求：某种审美之物通过解释、评论与批评成为艺术作品。
en: Three philosophical approaches have tried to explain such a movement. Dickie’s institutional theory would say that something becomes a work of art once it is in art institutions. But chairs, toilets and people are in there, and they are not artworks. Danto’s approach is to say that it is an object plus interpretation. And Adorno utters the requirement that something aesthetic becomes an artwork through interpretation, comment and criticism.

zh: 但所有这些都聚焦于审美对象的接受、审美经验，而忽视了生产方面。你如何说明艺术家所做的事？他们做什么？乍看之下，事情似乎简单：当艺术家工作时，她生产一件艺术作品。但这真的是工作吗？汉娜·阿伦特说：工作是再生产。但它是生产吗？艺术家所做之事的核心，是生产审美对象——可与珠宝、室内设计或精致烹饪相比吗？它是投资产品的制造式生产吗？是供消费的产品吗？还是供审美沉思的产品？
en: But all of these focus on the reception of an aesthetic object, on aesthetic experience, and neglect the productive aspect. How do you give an account for what artists do? What do they do? At first glance, things seem simple: when an artist works, she produces a work of art. But is it really work? Hannah Arendt says: work is reproduction. But is it production? Is the core of what artists do the production of aesthetic objects – comparable to jewellery, interior design or fine cooking? Is it a manufactory production of investment products? Products destined for consumption? Or for aesthetic contemplation?

zh: 这里有必要区分
实践与
实践。美学关注的是对感知方式的反思，包括对象、再现与审美判断。什么是审美实践？它不只是接受的实践——看、听、体验、解释一件作品、一顿饭、一处风景。
en: It is necessary to differentiate here between
and

practices. Aesthetics is concerned with the reflection on modes of perception, including objects, representations and aesthetic judgements. What are aesthetic practices? It is not just the practices of receiving – of seeing, listening, experiencing, interpreting a work, a meal, a view.

zh: 审美实践是那些关注我们感知事物方式的一切实践。它们构成对感知过程的反思，并准备审美判断（趣味判断）。然而，审美实践主要关切的不是这些判断，而首先是唤起并体验审美品质。
en: Aesthetic practices are all those where attention is paid to the way we perceive things. They form a reflection on perceptual processes and prepare aesthetic judgements (judgements of taste). However, aesthetic practices are not concerned primarily with these judgements, but first and foremost with evoking and experiencing aesthetic qualities.

zh: 烤蛋糕、品酒、游览名胜、设计花园、理发、化妆和冲咖啡——这些都是审美实践。它们不一定是职业活动，比如设计时装、装饰房屋、修建坟墓、制作纹身。作为一种审美活动，其目的不是赚钱或获得社会尊重。所有审美活动，无论是业余还是专业，无论是绘画与音乐还是陶艺与园艺，主要都不是以接受为目的。问题不在于感受愉悦或获得社会区隔。人们从事审美实践，不是为了达到这种效果，因为它不可由会产生同样效果的其他实践（如吸毒或沉浸式幻觉）替代。它本身就是目的：把注意力集中于感知方式。
en: Baking cakes, tasting wine, visiting places of interest, designing gardens, cutting hair, applying make-up and making coffee – these are all aesthetic practices. They are not necessarily professional activities, such as designing fashion, decorating houses, erecting graves, making tattoos. Their purpose, as an aesthetic activity, is not to make money or to gain social esteem. All aesthetic activities, amateur and professional, be it painting and music or pottery and gardening, are not primarily intended for reception. It is not about feeling pleasure or gaining social distinction. One performs an aesthetic practice not to achieve such an effect, because it is not replaceable by other practices that will have the same effect (as by taking drugs or by immersive illusion). But it is an end in itself: to focus attention on modes of perception.

zh: 对大多数审美实践来说，这一追求——把注意力集中于感知方式——是决定性要素。我们弹钢琴是为了弹钢琴，而不是为了听钢琴发出的声音。我做饭因为我爱做饭，而不只是为了喂饱自己。我画画因为我喜欢画画，而不是为了激起解释。审美活动的进行，是为了在对象上或情境中带出审美品质。实践的目标是活动本身，活动中的自发性要素在其中显现：把它进行下去。以风格、令人印象深刻的和谐与美丽形式呈现一件花艺，这些都是自发性的审美成就。它可归因于我，恰恰因为我并不确切知道它会是怎样，但我必须反思如何去做。
en: For most aesthetic practices, this quest – to focus attention on modes of perception – is the decisive element. We play piano in order to play piano, not to listen to the sound produced by the piano. I cook because I love to cook, not just to feed myself. I paint because I like to paint, not to stir interpretation. Aesthetic activities are carried out to bring out aesthetic qualities on an object or in a situation. The goal of the practice is the activity itself, in which the spontaneous element of the activity becomes manifest: to carry it out. Bringing out a floral arrangement with style, impressive harmony, beautiful form, these are spontaneous aesthetic achievements. It is attributable to me, precisely because I didn’t know exactly what it would be like, but I had to reflect on how to do it.

zh: 审美实践关联于一种特定构想：审美因素依赖于非审美品质的生产。审美效果由本身并非审美性的品质（就承载某一类感知判断而言）触发：形状、颜色、声音、体积。现在，即便自发性处于中心，也有两种“进行”方式：一种基于诀窍，另一种基于尝试。花艺布置或音乐作品的演绎，旨在重复和变化已知的非审美品质组合（花、音符）。许多审美实践满足于这种重复—变化，烹饪亦然。
en: Aesthetic practices are related to a specific vision of the dependence of aesthetic factors on the production of non-aesthetic qualities. Aesthetic effects are triggered by qualities that are not

es aesthetic (in the sense of carrying a certain type of perceptual judgement): shape, colour, sound, volume. Now, even if spontaneity is at the centre, there are two ways of ‘carrying out’: one based on know-how, the other on trying something out. The arrangement of flowers or the interpretation of a musical composition aims at the repetition and variation of already known combinations of non-aesthetic qualities (flowers, notes). Many aesthetic practices are sufficient in this repetition-variation, also cooking.

zh: 然而，艺术实践（也包括烹饪的艺术）超越了基于诀窍、模仿与练习的重复生产，因为它以这样一种构想为特征：一个最初仅属假设的审美效果，可能由新的、可能且可行的非审美品质类型之组合触发。换言之，艺术实践基于一个假设性的非审美品质组合方案。它基于尝试，基于实验性路径。
en: Artistic practice (also the art of cooking), however, goes beyond repeated production, based on know-how, on imitation and exercise, in so far as it is characterized by the vision of an initially hypothetical aesthetic effect that could be triggered by a combination of new, possible and feasible types of non-aesthetic qualities. In other words, artistic practice is based on the project of a hypothetical combination of non-aesthetic qualities. It is based on trying-out, on experimental approaches.

zh: 尼克·赞格威尔称之为“审美洞见”。
确实，所有艺术作品都包含审美品质，无论剂量多少，因此也都基于这种审美洞见。但设计、好莱坞和宝莱坞电影的创造过程也是如此。审美洞见使文化产业得以存活。它们并非艺行所特有。
en: Nick Zangwill calls this an ‘aesthetic insight’.

It is true that all works of art contain, in whatever dose, aesthetic qualities, and are therefore also based on such aesthetic insights. But the same goes for creative processes in design, in Hollywood and Bollywood film. Aesthetic insights keep the culture industry alive. They are not specific to arting.

zh: 因此，必须划出鲜明的区分。审美品质（美、优雅、丑）不是艺术作品的唯一品质——也许甚至不是决定性品质。与形式已完成、被塑造成具有功能性的日常对象不同，艺术作品被评价为“大胆、无礼、不敬、机智而聪明”（这些是丹托用来标示杜尚《泉》区别于小便池的那些品质的表述）。
这些品质归赋指向一种可能性的构想，而非实际的审美品质。因此，艺术标准与审美标准并不相同。审美品质是艺术作品（或多或少）可直接感知的品质：成功的形式、令人震惊的颜色、不协和的声音。另一方面，艺术品质，如机智与原创性，是一种关系性品质，意味着与其他事件相比较。审美品质可感知。艺术品质则不可直接感知。
en: Therefore it is important to draw a sharp distinction. Aesthetic qualities (beautiful, elegant, ugly) are not the only – or perhaps even the decisive – qualities of works of art. In contrast to everyday objects, which are formally finished and shaped to be functional, works of art are assessed as ‘daring, impudent, irreverent, witty and intelligent’ (these are the expressions with which Danto marks out the qualities by which Duchamp’s Fountain differs from a urinal).

These attributions of qualities address a vision of possibilities and not actual aesthetic quality. Artistic and aesthetic criteria are therefore not identical. Aesthetic quality is a (more or less) directly perceptible quality of a work of art: a successful form, a shocking colour, a dissonant sound. On the other hand, artistic quality, such as wit and originality, is a relational quality and implies a comparison with other events. Aesthetic qualities are perceptible. Artistic qualities are not directly perceptible.

zh: 把某物限定为“大胆、无礼、不敬、机智而聪明”，是通过认识性知识的形容语，区分出先于实现的理解、引导方案的理解。
标准是认识性的；它们相对于一个概念集合把某物挑选出来。因此，艺术活动并不止于审美品质的生产。“制作艺术”所需的那类理解，不只是可能的新方式据以促进审美品质的那类理解。那么，仅有“审美洞见”还不够。毋宁说，人们所寻求的，可以称之为一种
。在艺术构想中，审美洞见是必要但肯定不充分的条件，因为艺术作品不能凭审美品质与其他事物区分，至少不能仅凭审美品质。从杜尚和沃霍尔到挪用艺术与制度批判，这一点已被充分证明。
en: The qualification of something as ‘daring, impudent, irreverent, witty and intelligent’ distinguishes the understanding that precedes the realization, that which guides the project, by means of epithets of epistemic knowledge.

criteria are epistemic; they single something out in relation to a conceptual set. Artistic doing is therefore not exhausted in the production of aesthetic qualities. The kind of understanding that is needed to ‘make art’ is not only the kind of understanding on which possible new ways of encouraging aesthetic qualities are based. An ‘aesthetic insight’ is then just not enough. Rather, what is sought, one might say, is an

. In an artistic vision, aesthetic insight is a necessary but certainly not sufficient condition, since works of art cannot be distinguished from other things, or at least not exclusively, by aesthetic qualities. From Duchamp and Warhol to Appropriation Art and Institutional Critique, this has been fully demonstrated.

zh: 艺术性的实现只间接依赖于我们感官的组织。仅仅因为我素描、绘画、拍电影、押韵、写书、跳舞或弹钢琴，并不意味着我在“制作”艺术。也不是因为我在反身性的星丛中联结或组合材料，我就在制作艺术。
因为这些活动也出现在毫无艺术性的语境中（垃圾分类厂、纪录片、电子游戏、电视新闻）。这类活动，就为从零生产的非审美安排而组合材料并组织感官而言，当然可以参与艺术的创造，但它们不是、或不再是艺术活动的标志。艺术活动已从审美实践中解放出来。
en: An artistic realization is only indirectly dependent on the organization of our senses. Just because I draw, paint, make a film, rhyme, write a book, dance or play the piano does not mean that I ‘make’ art. Nor is it because I conjugate or combine material in a reflexive constellation that I make art.

Because the same activities also appear in contexts that have nothing artistic about them (waste separation plants, documentaries, video games, television news). Activities of this kind, in the sense of a combination of the material and the organization of the senses for

-produced non-aesthetic arrangements, can certainly be involved in the creation of art, but they are not, or no longer, the hallmarks of an artistic activity. Artist activity has emancipated itself from aesthetic practices.

zh: 艺术性在于某物如何被制作，而不在于某物以何种方式存在；最重要的是实践的转化。但“实践的转化”本身并不构成对艺术的规定，因为第一，这种转化必须使我们相信它带来了有雄心的质性革新（仅凭任性——例如决定不再用手画画、而用脚画画——是不够的）；第二，实践的艺术转化与公共空间的转化紧密相连，而公共空间始终以随机的、未参与其中的人在场为特征。一种在公共空间中的实践转化，如果同时旨在转化公共空间，就会成为艺术活动的合适规定。艺术不是密谋者共同体的事务，也不是这样一个机构的事务：其道路不容任何偏离。相反，它投入自由的接受，投入对判断可能性的实验：只有通过（匿名的）公众进行判断的可能性，才潜在地赋予一个事件以艺术地位。无论基于鉴赏家的知识，还是基于审美经验，还是基于非审美的接受（震惊、直觉），还是作为愉悦与欲望的自发表达：艺术只存在于公共空间中，存在于与既定公众的交锋中，存在于对某事物展开公共辩论的创造中，存在于对显现空间的重新配置中。正因如此，强调审美对象与艺术作品之间的过渡以再现或展出为标志，是正确的。
en: What is artistic is how something is made, not how something is something, and above all it is the transformation of the practice. But the ‘transformation of practice’ is not in itself a characterization of art, because, firstly, this transformation must convince us that it brings about an ambitious qualitative renovation (mere whim – for example, the decision to no longer paint with hands, but with feet – is not enough), and secondly, the artistic transformation of practice is closely linked to the transformation of public space, which is always characterized by the presence of random, uninvolved people. The transformation of a practice in public space would be a suitable qualification for artistic activity if it also aims at a transformation of the public space. Art is not the business of a community of conspirators; nor of an institution from the path of which nothing can deviate. On the contrary, it engages in free reception, in experimenting with the possibilities of judgement: only the possibility of judging through an (anonymous) public potentially confers the status of art on an event. Whether on the basis of a connoisseur’s knowledge, or on the basis of aesthetic experience, or on the basis of non-aesthetic reception (shock, intuition), or as a spontaneous expression of pleasure and desire: there is art only in the public space, in the confrontation with a given public, as the creation of a public debate about something, as the reconfiguration of the space of appearance. This is why it is right to stress that the passage between an aesthetic object and a work of art is marked by representation or exhibition.

zh: 尤莉安妮·雷本蒂施持对立观点。
对她而言，艺术作品本质上是对象经由经验而发生的反身性转化。据她说，这种转化不可控制，尤其因为经验指向外观，因而指向作品相对于其表演者的独立性。在外观中，对象向转化为艺术的过程敞开，并引发主体各种解释性与想象性的行动。这些行动作为审美判断被施行。
en: Juliane Rebentisch takes an opposing view.

For her, a work of art is essentially the reflexive transformation of an object through an experience. This transformation is uncontrollable, according to her, notably because experience refers to appearance, and therefore to the independence of works with regard to their performers. In appearance, objects open themselves to the process of transformation into art and give rise to all kinds of interpretative and imaginative acts by subjects. These are performed as aesthetic judgements.

zh: 但艺术作品之所以存在（哪怕只是作为“欣赏的候选者”），并不只是归功于制度，也不只是归功于经验或解释。艺术的对象或情境并非单纯被给予，而大多是形塑而成的，并需要被重新发明。艺术作品的体验并不是每个星期天再度指向同一组开放对象，而必须让自己暴露于某种尚无名称之物。
en: But it is not only thanks to the institution, nor only thanks to experience or interpretation, that works of art exist in the first place (be it only as ‘candidates for appreciation’). Art’s objects or situations are not simply given, but are mostly formed and need to be reinvented. The experience of artworks is not directed at the same set of open objects every Sunday, yet again, but needs to expose itself to something that has no name yet.

zh: 那么，艺术是生产我们无法辨认之物吗，正如阿多诺曾提出的那样？我们说，“制作艺术”就是完成一种艺术活动。但它真的是“做”或“制作”吗？完成是否意味着我随后生产了艺术，或我生产了艺术作品？不，严格来说，制作本身并不规定艺术活动，因为工作室助手或制作技师可以被委以这项任务，却不会因此成为艺术家。只要他们只生产别人所想象的东西，作品就不被归功于他们，即便他们最终因自己添加的品质而受到赞赏。细究之下，艺术家不是制作艺术的人。没有人通过完美复制而成为艺术家。即便独特之物的完美执行——技艺高超的助手或技师所能达到的那种——也不能使任何人成为艺术家。公众、观众常常是艺术作品生产的一部分——例如在互动性或关系性审美形式或观念艺术中。把艺术家提升到表演者与制作者群体之上的，是她关于某件待制作之物的观念，连同对一种新的制作
的发展。这不仅是相对于另一件艺术作品的新方式，而是相对于艺术的新方式。
en: Is art, then, the production of things we can’t identify, as Adorno once proposed? ‘To make art’, we said, is to accomplish an artistic activity. But is it really a ‘doing’ or ‘making’? Does the accomplishment imply that I then produce art or that I produce an artwork? No, strictly speaking the making itself does not characterize the artistic activity, because studio assistants or production technicians can be entrusted with the task without them becoming artists for all that. As long as they only produce what others have imagined, the work is not attributed to them, even if they are ultimately admired for the qualities they have added to it. On closer inspection, an artist is not the one who makes art. No one becomes an artist by perfectly copying. Even the perfect execution of the unique, such as can be achieved by highly skilled assistants or technicians, does not make anyone an artist. The public, the spectators, are often part of the production of the artwork – in interactive or relational aesthetic formats or conceptual art, for instance. What elevates an artist above the group of performers and manufacturers is her idea of something to be made, coupled with the development of a new
of making it. It is not just a new way with regard to another artwork, but to art.

zh: 所指向的首先是自发性的实现，一种新的生成方式。去艺行并不意味着制作或生产任何东西。它意味着进行自身的重新发明。
en: What is aimed at in
is above all a spontaneous realization, a new mode of becoming. To art does not mean to make or produce anything. It means to carry out a reinvention of itself.

zh: 艺术有一种特定历史，并不等同于文化史，因为它不断重新发明自身。因此，艺术必须在其概念制度与社会制度之外被寻找。它是一种否定性的动力学；正因如此，存在艺术，却没有作为单一整体的“艺术”——只有多元的、争竞性的进路。关于艺术将成为什么的争执，处于艺术概念的中心。
en: Art has a specific history, not identical with cultural history, because it is constantly reinventing itself. Art must therefore be sought outside its conceptual and social institutions. It is a dynamic of negation; and for this very reason there is art, but not ‘the art’ – only plural and agonal approaches. The quarrel about what art will become is at the centre of the concept of art.

zh: 因此，对艺术的概念进路的原创性，似乎成为艺术实践的一项要求。原创性是相对的标准。它是艺术作品的充分条件，但也许不是唯一条件。在这一点上，我不想被误解。此外，这里的原创性并不意味着“相同但不同”。艺术创造性产生一种新类型的观念、对象或事件。
具有艺术相关性的原创性是类型新颖性：它超越某一方面的单纯新颖或个体数目上的区别，最终指向概念转变。因为只有在一个艺术领域内、依照该领域现行的生成规则
不可能出现的东西，才能从艺术观点被视为原创：另一种说话方式，而不只是一个新短语。它将是某种会令所有熟悉现行生成规则、或对当代艺术有充分了解的人感到惊讶，甚至超出他们理解范围的东西。
en: The originality of their conceptual approach to art seems therefore to be a requirement for artistic practices. Originality is a relative criterion. It is a sufficient, but perhaps not the only, condition for works of art. I don’t want to be misunderstood on this point. Furthermore, originality here does not mean ‘same but different’. Artistic creativity gives rise to ideas or objects or events of a new kind.

Artistically relevant originality is genre novelty: it goes beyond the mere novelty of an aspect or numerical difference and ultimately aims at a conceptual shift. For only what could not have emerged

within an artistic field, and in accordance with the generative rules in force there, can be considered original from an artistic point of view: another way of speaking, and not just a new phrase. It will be something that will surprise, or even surpass, all those who are familiar with the generative rules in force, or who have sufficient information about contemporary art.

zh: 决定性要素是一种概念跃迁，它把所寻求之物或所应做之事从自身概念中提升出来，并为迄今为止从范畴观点被排除之物打开一道裂隙。借助概念跃迁，艺术过程应当被分析为其构成规则、规范与惯例、框定它们的制度以及作为参照点的目的的对象化否定。每一个微小的否定都促成艺术作品概念的转变，并最终促成艺术概念的转变。
en: The decisive element is a conceptual leap that elevates what is sought, or what ought to be done, out of its concept and opens a gap for what was hitherto excluded from a categorical point of view. With the conceptual leap, artistic processes should be analysed as the objectified negations of their constitutive rules, norms and conventions, of the institutions that frame them and of the purposes that serve as a point of reference. Every minuscule negation contributes to the transformation of the concept of the artwork, and ultimately the concept of art.

zh: 这种概念跃迁源于哲学实验。它们提供一种可能：相对于一个被证明不充分的感知图式，把握某种独异之物。如果艺术的首要取向是类型的新颖性，那不是因为它庆祝新颖，而是因为原初之物、新的类型是独异的、独特的——因为今天（仍然）独特的东西同时属于未来。
en: Such conceptual leaps stem from philosophical experimentation. They offer the possibility of apprehending something singular in contrast to a scheme of perception whose inadequacy is proven. If art is above all oriented towards the novelty of the genre, it is not because it celebrates novelty, but because the originary, the new genre is singular, unique – because what is (still) unique today is, at the same time, of the future.

zh: 如果艺术活动的主要定向点不是当代性，而是初始性、非存在、未来性，那么哲学实验就需要成为它的一部分。艺术哲学不应再指向完成的、对解释开放的艺术作品——如主流审美经验理论所认为的那样——而应指向在其原创性主张上有所作为的活动；也就是说，指向艺术的施行。艺术的这种生成——艺行——必须与工作、制作、行动分离，也与表演和解释分离，只要后者严格受制于规则、制度与结果。
en: If the main point of orientation of artistic activity is not contemporaneity, but initiality, inexistence, futurity, then philosophical experimentation needs to be part of it. Philosophy of art should no longer be directed towards finished works of art that are open to interpretation – as is the case under the dominant theories of aesthetic experience – but towards activities that make a difference in their claim to originality; that is, to the exercise of art. This becoming of art – arting – must be separated from work, from making, from action, but also from performance and interpretation, in so far as these are strictly subject to rules, institutions and result.

zh: 与经济创新的准则相比，激进的新是对构成规则的否定或变形。激进的新不是一个类别中的新要素；它作为无类别的聚集体而是新的。作为概念跃迁，它关联于自己所脱离之物，并且通过检验新的基础、规则与实施方式——这些不能从先前被认为有效的东西中推演出来——而做到这一点。激进想象显露于过程之中，而非产品之中。
en: Compared with the maxims of economic innovation, the radically new is the negation or metamorphosis of the constituent rules. The radically new is not a new element in a class; it is new as a conglomerate without classes. As a conceptual leap, it relates to what it stands out from, and moreover it does so by testing new bases, rules and modes of implementation that are non-deductible from what was known as valid before. It is in the process, not in the product, that radical imagination is revealed.

zh: 艺行作为一个过程，指一种（自我）创造性行动；它可以相对于研究者的系统性“发现”、工程师的发明、自然演化，以及设计师、理发师和厨师的职业创造性而被界定。它不是一种人确知如何施行的行动，而始终是在未知领域中的试错路径。艺行不遵从外部规定，甚至不遵从不断产出的律令，因为它是对失败可能性及这一可能性之条件的直面，是对实现之风险的直面。艺行不同于绘画、造型或音乐实践，不同于重复或即兴，因为像游戏一样，它就在自身的施行中完成。它不同于游戏之处在于，它不预设或实施具体规则，而总是从确立规则开始。在其他追求相对新意的职业创造性形式中（从炫技表演、新一季时尚到工程师的发明），艺行以缺乏任何适当性要求而区别开来。
en: Arting as a process refers to the (self-)creative action that can be delimited in relation to the systematic ‘findings’ of the researcher, the invention of the engineer, to natural evolution, to the professional creativity of designers, hairdressers and cooks. It is not an act which one knows firmly how to perform, but always a trial-and-error approach in the field of the unknown. Arting does not comply with external prescriptions, not even the imperative of productivity, because it is a confrontation with the possibility of failure and the condition of this possibility, with the risk of the realization. Arting differs from pictorial, plastic or musical practice, from repetition or improvisation because, like play, it is completed in accomplishment. It differs from play in that it does not suppose or implement concrete rules, but always begins by establishing them. Of the other forms of professional creativity in which one seeks the relatively new (from virtuoso performance, fashion for the new season, the engineer’s inventions), arting is distinguished by the absence of any requirement of adequacy.

zh: 必须为其发明满足适当性要求的审美实践，局限于对少数规则的可理解转化，以保持可识别性和可归属性。艺术不以同样方式受制于此。因为艺术中的新离开了既定概念、感知模式与行动形式的轨道。因此，艺术也要求悬置自我理解。这种悬置可能导致现实变得陌生，导致现实之外的东西影响感官，或导致某事在注意乃至感知的阈限之下发生并显现。对主体技术的否定、现实形式的改变以及构成规则的变形，可以被设想为内在的艺术行动。
en: Aesthetic practices that have to satisfy claims of adequacy for their inventions limit themselves to the comprehensible transformation of a few rules in order to remain recognizable and attributable. Art is not subject to this in the same way. For what is new in art goes off the rails of established concepts, patterns of perception and forms of action. Art therefore also requires a suspension of self-understanding. This suspension can result in reality becoming alien, in something other than reality affecting the senses, or in something happening and manifesting itself below the threshold of attention and even perception. The negation of the subject’s techniques, the change of form of the real and the metamorphosis of the constitutive rules can be conceived as intrinsic artistic acts.

zh: 那么，艺行不是绘画、雕塑、舞蹈、音乐、戏剧、写作和影像制作的总和或统称。不仅有个别艺术与个别艺术对象，还有作为一种艺术形式的艺行。
en: Arting, then, is not the sum of or generic term for painting, sculpture, dance, music, theatre, writing and video-making. There is not only individual arts and individual art objects, but also arting as an art form.

zh: 从更总体的层面思考，艺术实现——通过孤立、动员并模块化事件的品质——使某种在现实秩序中尚不算数之物行动。在探究成为现实的可能性时，它也探究非现实的前提。对艺行而言，一个艺术集体必须投入去现实化过程，并探究事件的前提及其可受影响性。艺术所特有的对时间可能性的检验，始于一种脱离过程：脱离归属，脱离固定的因果结构，脱离注意力装置，脱离延展或收缩当下的发生场域。
en: Thought in more global terms, artistic realization – by isolating, mobilizing and modularizing the qualities of events – makes something act that does not yet count in the order of reality. At the same time as it probes the possibilities of a becoming reality, it probes the presuppositions of irreality. For arting, an art collective must engage in a process of derealization and probe the presuppositions and the influenceability of events. The art-specific testing of temporal possibilities begins with the process of detachment with regard to belonging, with regard to fixed structures of cause and effect, with regard to devices of attention, with regard to fields of occurrence that extend or contract a present.

children: 艺行由此脱离其主体性、其文化、其传统、其在时间中的位置

zh: 。艺术性的去认同消解那些关系固着：它们执拗地使我们把某物看作某物、把某物看作另一物中的某物、看作方面的序列、意义的序列。当艺行方式集体地允许一种新的想象界时，也就是当它们发明现实之外的效果时，它们便是原初的。艺术的实现就是艺行：一种实现的展示，一次朝向未来性的伸展。

children: Arting thus detaches itself from its subjectivity, from its culture,
from its tradition, from its place in time

en: . Artistic disidentifications dissolve the fixations of relationships that obsessively make us see something as something, something in something, sequences of aspects, sequences of meaning. Ways of arting are originary when they allow, collectively, a new imaginary; that is to say, when they invent effects beyond reality. The realization of art is arting: the exhibition of a realization, an outreach toward futurity.

zh: 正如科内利乌斯·卡斯特里亚迪斯所表明的，现实只存在于一种激进想象的基础上，这种想象带出模式、形象与概念。
这恰恰不发生在艺术的新封建殿堂及其对全球当下的固着之中。
正是通过把艺行从它与媒介技术当下的策略、乃至与定义当代艺术的“当代”的缠绕中解放出来，我们才抵达未来艺术。因此，需要的是一种对当代性的哲学批判。从当代艺术迈向未来艺术的这一步，需要艺行哲学。
en: As Cornelius Castoriadis has shown, reality only exists on the basis of a radical imagination that brings out patterns, figures and concepts.
This does not happen precisely in the neo-feudal temples of art and their fixation on the global now.

It is by freeing arting from its intertwining with the strategies of the media-technological present, or even with the contemporary defining contemporary art, that we arrive at future art. What is needed is therefore a philosophical critique of contemporaneity. This step from contemporary to future art requires arting philosophy.

zh: 自主的思想、行动与感知只能在与非现实的关联中存在，现实正是从非现实中产生。因此，艺行也意味着一种内在于艺术的赋权过程：以艺术的未来之名，基于对形象／形式／图像的无条件创造，对迄今为止所实践之艺术的基础与规则进行批判。这一内在于艺术的艺行过程，是一项更总体的自主化工作的要素。
en: Autonomous thought, action and perception can only exist in connection with the unreal from which the real arises. Consequently, arting also implies a process of empowerment immanent to art: a critique of the foundations and rules of the art practised so far, based on the unconditional creation of figures/ forms/images, in the name of a future of art. This process of arting, immanent to art, is an element of a more global work of autonomization.

zh: 艺术是一种自由的实现。一种能够实现这一点的艺术哲学，因此是艺术实践的组成部分。
en: Art is a free realization. A philosophy of art that achieves this is therefore an integral part of artistic practice.
